Below is a quick‑reference list of the **federal public holidays that create long weekends in Canada during 2023**.  
(If a holiday falls on a weekend, the “observed” date is the following Monday, and the long‑weekend period is shown accordingly.)

| Holiday | 2023 Date | Observed (if weekend) | Long‑Weekend Period |
|---------|-----------|-----------------------|---------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 (Sunday) | Jan 2 (Monday) | Dec 31 2022 – Jan 2 2023 |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 (Friday) | Apr 7 | Apr 7 – Apr 9 |
| Victoria Day | May 22 (Monday) | May 22 | May 20 – May 22 |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 (Saturday) | Jul 3 (Monday) | Jul 1 – Jul 3 |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 (Monday) | Sep 4 | Sep 2 – Sep 4 |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 (Monday) | Oct 9 | Oct 7 – Oct 9 |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 (Friday) | Nov 11 | Nov 11 – Nov 13 |
| Christmas Day | Dec 25 (Monday) | Dec 25 | Dec 23 – Dec 25 |

> **Note:**  
> • These are the federal holidays that are observed nationwide.  
> • Many provinces have additional holidays (e.g., Family Day, St. Patrick’s Day, Heritage Day, etc.) that can create extra long weekends.  
> • If you need province‑specific long‑weekend lists, let me know which province(s) you’re interested in and I can provide those details.
